**Java – A quick primer** | Topic | What you’ll learn | |-------|-------------------| | **What is it?** | Java is a high‑level, class‑based, object‑oriented programming language designed with the philosophy “write once, run anywhere” (WORA). It was created by James Gosling at Sun Microsystems (now owned by Oracle) and released publicly in 1995. | | **Core idea** | Code compiled into bytecode runs on the Java Virtual Machine (JVM), allowing the same program to execute on Windows, macOS, Linux, Android devices, embedded systems, servers, and more without modification. | | **Key characteristics** | • Strongly typed
• Automatic memory management (garbage collection)
• Rich standard library (java.lang.*, java.util.* …)
• Threaded concurrency support
• Security sandbox (especially important for applets & web apps)
• Platform independence via JVM | | **Typical use cases** | • Web application backends (Spring Boot, Jakarta EE)
• Enterprise software (ERP, CRM, banking platforms)
• Mobile apps (Android SDK)
• Desktop GUIs (Swing, JavaFX)
• Big‑data processing (Apache Hadoop, Spark)
• Embedded/IoT devices (Arduino, Raspberry Pi libraries)
• Game development (LibGDX, jMonkeyEngine) | | **Evolution timeline** | *1991–95*: Development → JDK 1.0 release.
*2002*: Java 2 Platform, Standard Edition (J2SE) becomes Java SE 5.0 (introduces generics, annotations, enhanced enums).
*2018*: Java 9 introduces modules (Project Jigsaw).
*2020s*: Regular six‑month releases (e.g., Java 17 LTS, Java 21 upcoming). | | **Syntax basics** | ```java\npublic class HelloWorld {\n public static void main(String[] args) {\n System.out.println(\"Hello, world!\");\n }\n}\n``` | | **Compilation vs execution** | `javac MyClass.java` ➜ compiles to `MyClass.class`.
`java MyClass` ➜ loads `.class`, interprets bytecode via JVM. | | **Popular frameworks/libraries** | Spring/Spring Boot, Hibernate/JPA, Apache Commons, Jackson, Logback, Mockito, TestNG/JUnit, Vaadin, Play Framework. | | **Learning resources** | • Official docs: https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/
• Online courses: Coursera’s “Java Programming”, Udemy’s “Java Mastery”, freeCodeCamp YouTube tutorials.
• Books: “Effective Java” (Joshua Bloch), “Head First Java”. | ### Quick FAQ | Question | Answer | |----------|--------| | **Why still popular after all these years?** | Mature ecosystem, huge community, robust performance, strong tooling (IntelliJ IDEA, Eclipse), extensive enterprise adoption, continuous evolution. | | **Can I write mobile apps directly in Java?** | Yes—Android apps were historically written entirely in Java until Kotlin became the preferred choice. Many legacy Android projects remain pure Java. | | **How does garbage collection work?** | The JVM periodically identifies objects no longer referenced from active code paths and frees their memory automatically, reducing manual memory errors. | | **Is Java safe?** | Generally yes; its type system prevents many bugs, and the JVM enforces strict access controls. However, like any platform, security depends on proper coding practices and timely updates. | | **Do I need a license?** | No. Since Java 11, Oracle offers open source builds under the GPLv2+CE license. Other vendors provide fully compatible runtimes (OpenJDK, Amazon Corretto, Azul Zulu, AdoptOpenJDK). | --- #### TL;DR *Java is a versatile, mature, cross‑platform programming language used everywhere—from server‐side applications and Android phones to big data pipelines and IoT gadgets. Its design around the JVM gives developers portability, while its rich ecosystem keeps it relevant today.*
